mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has moved from -18.4 to -15.0 to -16.6 to -16.1 over the last four weeks, showing a shallow recovery trend off its trough. This gradual mean-reversion toward baseline is expected to continue, producing a higher four-week mean than the prior period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -18.4 at t-3w to -15.0 at t-2w before partial pullback
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the trailing 28-day mean, the mean-reversion mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES dropped sharply from -22.1 to -30.9 in the latest week, an 8.8-point week-on-week decline consistent with a holiday-driven closure (e.g., Oct 12 national holiday falling inside the window). This temporary suppression of commuting activity will depress weekday retail footfall for roughly one week before normalizing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeds 8 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -22.1 to -30.9 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the following week is flat or higher than the prior week despite the WORKPLACES breach, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-18.6) and WORKPLACES (-30.9) both fell sharply in the same week while RESIDENTIAL rose to 3.0, jointly indicating a holiday pause rather than genuine demand destruction. Once TRANSIT and WORKPLACES simultaneously rebound in subsequent weeks, pent-up shopping and leisure trips will push RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise in the same week following the joint holiday-week decline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both declined sharply in the same week as RESIDENTIAL rose
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together but RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked to +23.4 in the latest week, likely reflecting unseasonably mild October weather that diverts leisure trips outdoors and away from indoor retail. As autumn temperatures decline over the next month, outdoor substitution will fade and displaced leisure demand will shift back into retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 23.4 in the most recent week, its highest value in the snapshot
regime_hint: early-autumn mild-weather transitioning to cooler weather
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated above 20% for the next four weeks without any corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC, the seasonal substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM fell sharply from 7.4 to 0.4, crossing near its baseline level, likely due to temporary holiday closures of essential retail. Because grocery and pharmacy demand is inelastic, this dip should rebound quickly, and the rebound in essential-trip mobility typically co-moves with a rebound in broader retail and recreation activity within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean falls below 2 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped from 7.4 to 0.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rebounds in the next week but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to its trailing 28-day mean, the co-movement mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has gradually increased from 1.4 to 1.6 to 3.0 over the last three weeks, indicating a sustained rise in time spent at home. This behavioral shift toward home-centered activity is expected to continue crowding out discretionary retail and recreation outings over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 1.4 to 1.6 to 3.0 over the last three weekly readings
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues rising but RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is higher than its trailing mean, the crowding-out mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility remains above the 20% threshold for two consecutive weeks, continued favorable outdoor conditions will keep diverting leisure trips from retail venues until the seasonal transition (shortening days, clock change) forces a shift back indoors, at which point RETAIL_REC should rise as holiday-shopping-season behavior begins.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean remains above 20 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 23.4 in the latest week after 18.4 two weeks prior
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above 20% for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not exceed the trailing mean, the seasonal-transition mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Despite WORKPLACES falling to -30.9, RETAIL_REC has remained relatively stable around -16, suggesting retail demand has decoupled from office-commute patterns amid entrenched remote/hybrid work. In this decoupled regime, continued weakness in WORKPLACES will not translate into further RETAIL_REC decline, and RETAIL_REC may even drift upward as consumers substitute commute-linked trips with dedicated shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -25 percentage points while RETAIL_REC stays within plus/minus 2 points of its recent mean
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -30.9 while RETAIL_REC held near -16 in the same week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays deeply negative and RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean falls below its trailing mean, the decoupling mechanism is rejected.
